metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in late January to assess progress. Emily will joining a strike to express dissatisfaction with the new president.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Zimbabwe strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 20th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have we decided on a date for the joint meeting? I was thinking January 20th could work well. What do you think?  

Also… I heard about Emily joining a strike. Is that a common thing to discuss or participate in for protests? It’s not something I see happening in my culture.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 20th sounds... fine. We should confirm it with everyone involved, though. 

As for strikes... uh, in my culture, we don’t really join protests like that. It’s just not something we do. We prefer to handle issues differently, I guess. I don't see the value in strikes.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, confirming with everyone is important. I hope they agree on January 20th.  

About the strikes... I just don’t understand how discussing or joining protests can lead to positive outcomes. Don’t you think it could create more conflict instead of resolving issues?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out in their own ways. I don't really see meaningful differences here. It's just how things go sometimes. 

Anyway, I think confirming January 20th is a good step forward. Let's make sure we get that locked in with everyone for the meeting.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
Definitely, locking in January 20th is a priority. I’ll reach out to the others as soon as possible.  

But I still find it hard to believe that strikes can really bring about change. Don’t you think there are better ways to express dissatisfaction?

I agree, there are better ways to express dissatisfaction. Strikes can lead to more problems than solutions. In my culture, we focus on dialogue and finding common ground instead. 

Let’s keep our attention on the meeting. January 20th needs to be set, and that’s our priority right now.
turns.label: Acceptance
